claim: Oligodendrocytes and their progenitors upregulate MHC pathways in response to inflammation.
source: Oligodendrocytes and their progenitors upregulate MHC pathways in response to inflammation, but the frequency of this phenotypic change is unknown and the features of these immune oligodendroglia are poorly defined.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as an established observation that motivates the study.

claim: The frequency of MHC pathway upregulation in oligodendroglia is unknown.
source: Oligodendrocytes and their progenitors upregulate MHC pathways in response to inflammation, but the frequency of this phenotypic change is unknown and the features of these immune oligodendroglia are poorly defined.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states this knowledge gap.

claim: The features of immune oligodendroglia are poorly defined.

claim: MHC class I and II transgenic reporter mice were generated to define the dynamics of MHC activation in response to inflammatory demyelination.
source: We generated MHC class I and II transgenic reporter mice to define their dynamics in response to inflammatory demyelination, providing a means to monitor MHC activation in diverse cell types in living mice and define their roles in aging, injury, and disease.
evidence: The abstract describes the generation of these reporter mice as a primary contribution of the study.

claim: The reporter mice provide a means to monitor MHC activation in diverse cell types in living mice.
source: We generated MHC class I and II transgenic reporter mice to define their dynamics in response to inflammatory demyelination, providing a means to monitor MHC activation in diverse cell types in living mice and define their roles in aging, injury, and disease.
evidence: The abstract states this as a capability of the generated reporter mice.

claim: Some oligodendroglia in mouse inflammatory models express transcripts associated with MHC antigen presenting and processing pathways.
source: Single-cell and single-nucleus RNA sequencing has revealed that some oligodendroglia in both mouse inflammatory models (Falcão et al., 2018; Meijer et al., 2022) and human multiple sclerosis (MS) (Schirmer et al., 2019; Jäkel et al., 2019; Absinta et al., 2021) express transcripts associated with major histocompatibility complex (MHC) antigen presenting and processing pathways.
evidence: The introduction cites published studies demonstrating this finding.

claim: Some oligodendroglia in human multiple sclerosis express transcripts associated with MHC antigen presenting and processing pathways.
source: Single-cell and single-nucleus RNA sequencing has revealed that some oligodendroglia in both mouse inflammatory models (Falcão et al., 2018; Meijer et al., 2022) and human multiple sclerosis (MS) (Schirmer et al., 2019; Jäkel et al., 2019; Absinta et al., 2021) express transcripts associated with major histocompatibility complex (MHC) antigen presenting and processing pathways.
evidence: The introduction cites published studies demonstrating this finding in human MS.

claim: Immune oligodendrocyte precursor cells (iOPCs) and oligodendrocytes (iOLs) have been detected in Alzheimer's disease.
source: These immune oligodendrocyte precursor cells (iOPCs) and oligodendrocytes (iOLs) have been detected in Alzheimer's disease (Lau et al., 2020) and viral infection models (Pan et al., 2020; Malone et al., 2008; Phares et al., 2009), and can be induced by exposure to interferon-γ (IFN-γ), suggesting that some oligodendroglia undergo this distinct phenotypic change in response to inflammation.
evidence: The introduction cites a published study showing iOPCs/iOLs in Alzheimer's disease.

claim: Immune oligodendrocyte precursor cells (iOPCs) and oligodendrocytes (iOLs) have been detected in viral infection models.
source: These immune oligodendrocyte precursor cells (iOPCs) and oligodendrocytes (iOLs) have been detected in Alzheimer's disease (Lau et al., 2020) and viral infection models (Pan et al., 2020; Malone et al., 2008; Phares et al., 2009), and can be induced by exposure to interferon-γ (IFN-γ), suggesting that some oligodendroglia undergo this distinct phenotypic change in response to inflammation.
evidence: The introduction cites published studies showing iOPCs/iOLs in viral infection models.

evidence: The introduction states this as an established finding.

claim: Some oligodendroglia undergo a distinct phenotypic change in response to inflammation.

evidence: The introduction infers this from the cited evidence about iOPCs/iOLs.

claim: The role of immune oligodendroglia is unknown.
source: The role of these immune oligodendroglia is unknown (Harrington et al., 2020), but their presence raises the possibility that oligodendroglia may present antigens to T cells, be subject to cytotoxic CD8 T cell-mediated death (Kirby et al., 2019) and perpetuate the immune response through release of cytokines and interactions with CD4 T cells.
evidence: The introduction explicitly states this knowledge gap.

claim: Oligodendroglia may present antigens to T cells.
source: The role of these immune oligodendroglia is unknown (Harrington et al., 2020), but their presence raises the possibility that oligodendroglia may present antigens to T cells, be subject to cytotoxic CD8 T cell-mediated death (Kirby et al., 2019) and perpetuate the immune response through release of cytokines and interactions with CD4 T cells.
evidence: The introduction presents this as a speculative possibility based on their MHC expression.

claim: Oligodendroglia may be subject to cytotoxic CD8 T cell-mediated death.
source: The role of these immune oligodendroglia is unknown (Harrington et al., 2020), but their presence raises the possibility that oligodendroglia may present antigens to T cells, be subject to cytotoxic CD8 T cell-mediated death (Kirby et al., 2019) and perpetuate the immune response through release of cytokines and interactions with CD4 T cells.
evidence: The introduction presents this as a speculative possibility with citation support.

claim: Oligodendroglia may perpetuate the immune response through release of cytokines and interactions with CD4 T cells.

evidence: The introduction presents this as a speculative possibility.

claim: Oligodendroglial death or inflammation could contribute to impaired remyelination seen in MS and other progressive diseases.
source: This oligodendroglial death or inflammation could contribute to impaired remyelination seen in MS and other progressive diseases (Lubetzki et al., 2020; Mahad et al., 2015; Lassmann et al., 2012).

claim: Further exploration of the spatial and temporal dynamics of iOPCs/iOLs have been limited by their relative rarity.
source: Further exploration of the spatial and temporal dynamics of iOPCs/iOLs have been limited by their relative rarity and our inability to identify which cells have transformed in living tissue.
evidence: The introduction states this as a limitation in the field.

claim: Two novel MHC I and MHC II reporter mouse lines were generated that express tdTomato when MHC pathways are activated.
source: To enable detection of which cells upregulate MHC pathways in vivo, we generated two novel MHC I and MHC II reporter mouse lines that express tdTomato when these pathways are activated, and used these lines to define their incidence and transcriptional characteristics in two mouse models of inflammatory demyelination.
evidence: The introduction describes the generation of these reporter mice as a primary contribution.

claim: The reporter mouse lines were used to define the incidence and transcriptional characteristics of immune oligodendroglia in two mouse models of inflammatory demyelination.
source: To enable detection of which cells upregulate MHC pathways in vivo, we generated two novel MHC I and MHC II reporter mouse lines that express tdTomato when these pathways are activated, and used these lines to define their incidence and transcriptional characteristics in two mouse models of inflammatory demyelination.
evidence: The introduction describes the use of these mice in the study.

claim: MHC class II chaperone invariant chain (Cd74 or Ii) is a required component of the antigen processing/presentation machinery.
source: MHC class II chaperone invariant chain (Cd74 or Ii) and MHC class I component beta-2-microglobulin (B2m) are required components of the antigen processing/presentation machinery that are expressed by a subset of oligodendroglia in mouse inflammatory models (Falcão et al., 2018) and human MS brain (Schirmer et al., 2019; Jäkel et al., 2019).
evidence: The results section states this as established knowledge.

claim: MHC class I component beta-2-microglobulin (B2m) is a required component of the antigen processing/presentation machinery.

evidence: The results section states this as established knowledge.

claim: Cd74 and B2m are expressed by a subset of oligodendroglia in mouse inflammatory models.

claim: B2m and Cd74 genes were targeted for the generation of MHC class I and MHC class II reporter mice, respectively.
source: We chose to target B2m and Cd74 genes for the generation of MHC class I and MHC class II reporter mice, respectively, as both of these transcripts are upregulated in oligodendroglia in response to IFN-γ treatment (Kirby et al., 2019), and both transcripts are present in inflammatory oligodendroglia in mouse inflammatory models (Falcão et al., 2018) and human MS tissue (Schirmer et al., 2019; Jäkel et al., 2019).
evidence: The results section describes the rationale for gene selection.

claim: B2m and Cd74 transcripts are upregulated in oligodendroglia in response to IFN-γ treatment.
source: We chose to target B2m and Cd74 genes for the generation of MHC class I and MHC class II reporter mice, respectively, as both of these transcripts are upregulated in oligodendroglia in response to IFN-γ treatment (Kirby et al., 2019), and both transcripts are present in inflammatory oligodendroglia in mouse inflammatory models (Falcão et al., 2018) and human MS tissue (Schirmer et al., 2019; Jäkel et al., 2019).
evidence: The results section cites a published study demonstrating this.

claim: B2m and Cd74 transcripts are present in inflammatory oligodendroglia in mouse inflammatory models.

evidence: The results section cites published studies demonstrating this.

claim: B2m and Cd74 transcripts are present in inflammatory oligodendroglia in human MS tissue.
source: We chose to target B2m and Cd74 genes for the generation of MHC class I and MHC class II reporter mice, respectively, as both of these transcripts are upregulated in oligodendroglia in response to IFN-γ treatment (Kirby et al., 2019), and both transcripts are present in inflammatory oligodendroglia in mouse inflammatory models (Falcão et al., 2018) and human MS tissue (Schirmer et al., 2019; Jäkel et al., 2019).
evidence: The results section cites published studies demonstrating this.

claim: CRISPR/Cas9-mediated gene editing was used to replace the stop codon of B2m and Cd74 genes with a P2A-TdTomato-WPRE-pA sequence.
source: To facilitate identification of these cells, we used CRISPR/Cas9-mediated gene editing to replace the stop codon of these genes with a P2A-TdTomato-WPRE-pA sequence (Figure 1A-C), generating B2m-tdTomato (B2mtdT) and Cd74-tdTomato (Cd74tdT) reporter mice in which 2A cleaving self-peptide facilitates cleavage of tdTomato from the endogenous protein without disrupting expression of the endogenous genes (Figure 1—figure supplement 1) or antigen presentation (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The results section describes the method used to generate the reporter mice, with reference to Figure 1A-C.

claim: 2A cleaving self-peptide facilitates cleavage of tdTomato from the endogenous protein without disrupting expression of the endogenous genes.
source: To facilitate identification of these cells, we used CRISPR/Cas9-mediated gene editing to replace the stop codon of these genes with a P2A-TdTomato-WPRE-pA sequence (Figure 1A-C), generating B2m-tdTomato (B2mtdT) and Cd74-tdTomato (Cd74tdT) reporter mice in which 2A cleaving self-peptide facilitates cleavage of tdTomato from the endogenous protein without disrupting expression of the endogenous genes (Figure 1—figure supplement 1) or antigen presentation (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The results section states this mechanism with reference to supplementary figures showing data.

claim: In B2mtdT reporter mice, tdT was ubiquitously expressed in all immune cells analyzed in the spleen.
source: In B2mtdT reporter mice, tdT was ubiquitously expressed in all immune cells analyzed in the spleen (Figure 1D) and tdT fluorescent cells were immunoreactive to B2m (Figure 1E).
evidence: The results section describes this observation with reference to Figure 1D showing flow cytometry data.

claim: tdT fluorescent cells in B2mtdT mice were immunoreactive to B2m.
source: In B2mtdT reporter mice, tdT was ubiquitously expressed in all immune cells analyzed in the spleen (Figure 1D) and tdT fluorescent cells were immunoreactive to B2m (Figure 1E).
evidence: The results section describes this observation with reference to Figure 1E showing immunostaining data.

claim: In Cd74tdT reporter mice, tdT expression was highest in professional antigen presenting cells, such as dendritic cells and B cells.
source: In Cd74tdT reporter mice, tdT expression was highest in professional antigen presenting cells, such as dendritic cells and B cells (Figure 1F) and tdT fluorescent cells were immunoreactive to CD74 (Figure 1G).
evidence: The results section describes this observation with reference to Figure 1F showing flow cytometry data.

claim: tdT fluorescent cells in Cd74tdT mice were immunoreactive to CD74.
source: In Cd74tdT reporter mice, tdT expression was highest in professional antigen presenting cells, such as dendritic cells and B cells (Figure 1F) and tdT fluorescent cells were immunoreactive to CD74 (Figure 1G).
evidence: The results section describes this observation with reference to Figure 1G showing immunostaining data.

claim: Cd74 has diverse roles in cell survival, migration and MIF cytokine signaling independent of MHC class II.
source: Independent of MHC class II, Cd74 has diverse roles in cell survival, migration and MIF (macrophage migration inhibitory factor) cytokine signaling (Su et al., 2017; Schröder, 2016).
evidence: The results section cites published studies describing these functions.

claim: I-A/I-E co-expression with tdT was highest in dendritic cells and B cells in Cd74tdT mice.
source: I-A/I-E co-expression with tdT was highest in dendritic cells and B cells (Figure 1H) and monocytes that exhibited intermediate tdT fluorescence were also negative or weakly immunoreactive for I-A/I-E expression (Figure 1H), indicating that the level of tdT expression correlates well with MHC class II receptor expression.
evidence: The results section describes this observation with reference to Figure 1H showing flow cytometry data.

claim: Monocytes that exhibited intermediate tdT fluorescence in Cd74tdT mice were also negative or weakly immunoreactive for I-A/I-E expression.
source: I-A/I-E co-expression with tdT was highest in dendritic cells and B cells (Figure 1H) and monocytes that exhibited intermediate tdT fluorescence were also negative or weakly immunoreactive for I-A/I-E expression (Figure 1H), indicating that the level of tdT expression correlates well with MHC class II receptor expression.
evidence: The results section describes this observation with reference to Figure 1H showing flow cytometry data.

claim: The level of tdT expression correlates well with MHC class II receptor expression in Cd74tdT mice.
source: I-A/I-E co-expression with tdT was highest in dendritic cells and B cells (Figure 1H) and monocytes that exhibited intermediate tdT fluorescence were also negative or weakly immunoreactive for I-A/I-E expression (Figure 1H), indicating that the level of tdT expression correlates well with MHC class II receptor expression.
evidence: The results section infers this correlation from the flow cytometry data in Figure 1H.

claim: IFN-γ is sufficient to induce MHC class I and II expression in oligodendroglia in vitro.
source: To determine whether reporter expression is induced in glial cells, immunopanned reporter expressing glial cells were cultured with and without IFN-γ, as we have previously shown that IFN-γ is sufficient to induce MHC class I and II expression in oligodendroglia in vitro (Kirby et al., 2019).
evidence: The results section cites a previous study demonstrating this.

claim: IFN-γ increased tdT expression in Olig2+ cells in OPC enriched cultures from both B2mtdT and Cd74tdT mice.
source: Consistent with this observation, IFN-γ increased tdT expression in Olig2 immunoreactive (+) cells in OPC enriched cultures (Fancy et al., 2011) from both B2mtdT and Cd74tdT (Figure 1I–J).
evidence: The results section describes this observation with reference to Figure 1I-J showing culture data.

claim: In Cd74tdT glial cultures treated with IFN-γ, tdT expression was found in Iba1+ microglia and GFAP+ astrocytes.
source: In Cd74tdT glial cultures treated with IFN-γ, tdT expression was also found in Iba1+ microglia and GFAP+ astrocytes (Figure 1K).
evidence: The results section describes this observation with reference to Figure 1K showing immunostaining data.

claim: In Cd74tdT mice, tdT expression was most prevalent in the meninges and choroid plexus of adult CNS.
source: To characterize the adult central nervous system (CNS) baseline MHC expression, we evaluated the brain, spinal cord, and retinal tissues of adult Cd74tdT and B2mtdT reporter mice. In Cd74tdT mice, tdT expression was most prevalent in the meninges and choroid plexus (Figure 2A–D), but was also observed within some microglia in the ventral brain (Figure 2B and E).
evidence: The results section describes this observation with reference to Figure 2A-D showing tissue imaging.

claim: In Cd74tdT mice, tdT expression was observed within some microglia in the ventral brain.
source: To characterize the adult central nervous system (CNS) baseline MHC expression, we evaluated the brain, spinal cord, and retinal tissues of adult Cd74tdT and B2mtdT reporter mice. In Cd74tdT mice, tdT expression was most prevalent in the meninges and choroid plexus (Figure 2A–D), but was also observed within some microglia in the ventral brain (Figure 2B and E).
evidence: The results section describes this observation with reference to Figure 2B and E showing tissue imaging.

claim: tdT expression co-localized with I-A/I-E and Cd74 expression in the meninges and choroid plexus of Cd74tdT mice.
source: tdT expression co-localized with I-A/I-E (Figure 2A–C) and Cd74 (Figure 2C) expression in the meninges and choroid plexus.
evidence: The results section describes this observation with reference to Figure 2A-C showing immunostaining data.

claim: In the CNS of B2mtdT mice, tdT expression was prominent in endothelial cells and microglia throughout the brain, spinal cord, and retina.
source: In the CNS of B2mtdT mice, tdT expression was prominent in endothelial cells and microglia throughout the brain, spinal cord, and retina (Figure 3A–G).
evidence: The results section describes this observation with reference to Figure 3A-G showing tissue imaging.

claim: Some neurons in the cerebellum, septum, hippocampus, and cortex of B2mtdT mice expressed tdT.
source: In addition, some neurons in the cerebellum, septum, hippocampus, and cortex expressed tdT (Figure 3H–L).
evidence: The results section describes this observation with reference to Figure 3H-L showing tissue imaging.

claim: Within the corpus callosum and cortex of B2mtdT mice, there was diffuse parenchymal expression of tdT in addition to microglial and endothelial cell expression.
source: Within the corpus callosum and cortex, in addition to microglial and endothelial cell expression, there was diffuse parenchymal expression of tdT (Figure 3A–C), possibly arising from projections of tdT+ neurons.
evidence: The results section describes this observation with reference to Figure 3A-C showing tissue imaging.

claim: Diffuse parenchymal tdT expression in B2mtdT corpus callosum and cortex possibly arises from projections of tdT+ neurons.
source: Within the corpus callosum and cortex, in addition to microglial and endothelial cell expression, there was diffuse parenchymal expression of tdT (Figure 3A–C), possibly arising from projections of tdT+ neurons.
evidence: The results section speculates about the source of this expression based on the observation of tdT+ neurons.

claim: Expression of MHC class I by neurons may allow them to present antigen and render them more prone to death in inflammatory conditions.
source: Expression of MHC class I by these neurons may allow them to present antigen and render them more prone to death in inflammatory conditions.
evidence: The results section speculates about the functional implications of neuronal MHC class I expression.

claim: With increasing EAE clinical score, there was a concomitant increase in tdT expression in spinal cord lesion areas in both B2mtdT and Cd74tdT animals.
source: Reporter mice subjected to MOG35-55 EAE were sacrificed with EAE presentation ranging from pre-clinical (score 0), tail and hindlimb weakness (score 1–2.5) to complete hindlimb paralysis (score 3–4). With increasing EAE clinical score, there was a concomitant increase in tdT expression in spinal cord lesion areas in both B2mtdT (Figure 4A) and Cd74tdT animals (Figure 4B).
evidence: The results section describes this observation with reference to Figure 4A and 4B showing tissue imaging.

claim: tdT was present in EAE ventral brain meningeal cell clusters and corpus callosum cell clusters in Cd74tdT and B2mtdT animals.
source: tdT was also present in EAE ventral brain meningeal cell clusters and corpus callosum cell clusters in Cd74tdT and B2mtdT animals (Figure 5A–F).
evidence: The results section describes this observation with reference to Figure 5A-F showing tissue imaging.

claim: tdT was expressed in both infiltrating myeloid cells and microglia in B2mtdT and Cd74tdT EAE brain.
source: tdT was expressed in both infiltrating myeloid cells and microglia in B2mtdT and Cd74tdT EAE brain (Figure 5G).
evidence: The results section describes this observation with reference to Figure 5G showing immunostaining data.

claim: Infiltrating myeloid cells and microglia exhibited tdT expression in the brain and spinal cord of Cd74tdT mice with EAE.
source: When analyzed by flow cytometry, infiltrating myeloid cells and microglia exhibited tdT expression in the brain and spinal cord of Cd74tdT mice with EAE (Figure 6A and B) and both the proportion of myeloid cells and microglia that expressed tdT (Figure 6A), and the level of tdT expression by these cells (Figure 6B), were higher in co-stimulatory molecule expressing cells compared to non-co-stimulatory molecule expressing cells.
evidence: The results section describes this observation with reference to Figure 6A and B showing flow cytometry data.

claim: The proportion of myeloid cells and microglia that expressed tdT in Cd74tdT EAE mice was higher in co-stimulatory molecule expressing cells compared to non-co-stimulatory molecule expressing cells.
source: When analyzed by flow cytometry, infiltrating myeloid cells and microglia exhibited tdT expression in the brain and spinal cord of Cd74tdT mice with EAE (Figure 6A and B) and both the proportion of myeloid cells and microglia that expressed tdT (Figure 6A), and the level of tdT expression by these cells (Figure 6B), were higher in co-stimulatory molecule expressing cells compared to non-co-stimulatory molecule expressing cells.
evidence: The results section describes this observation with reference to Figure 6A showing flow cytometry data.

claim: The level of tdT expression by myeloid cells and microglia in Cd74tdT EAE mice was higher in co-stimulatory molecule expressing cells compared to non-co-stimulatory molecule expressing cells.
source: When analyzed by flow cytometry, infiltrating myeloid cells and microglia exhibited tdT expression in the brain and spinal cord of Cd74tdT mice with EAE (Figure 6A and B) and both the proportion of myeloid cells and microglia that expressed tdT (Figure 6A), and the level of tdT expression by these cells (Figure 6B), were higher in co-stimulatory molecule expressing cells compared to non-co-stimulatory molecule expressing cells.
evidence: The results section describes this observation with reference to Figure 6B showing flow cytometry data.

claim: In B2mtdT mouse brain, the percentage of tdT expressing microglia was not significantly different between M1 or M2 microglia.
source: In B2mtdT mouse brain, the percentage of tdT expressing microglia was not significantly different between M1 or M2 microglia, defined by CD86 and CD206 expression, respectively (Jurga et al., 2020; Figure 6C and D); however, M1 microglia had significantly higher tdT fluorescence compared to M2 and M1-2 microglia (Figure 5E).
evidence: The results section describes this observation with reference to Figure 6C and D showing flow cytometry data.

claim: M1 microglia in B2mtdT mouse brain had significantly higher tdT fluorescence compared to M2 and M1-2 microglia.
source: In B2mtdT mouse brain, the percentage of tdT expressing microglia was not significantly different between M1 or M2 microglia, defined by CD86 and CD206 expression, respectively (Jurga et al., 2020; Figure 6C and D); however, M1 microglia had significantly higher tdT fluorescence compared to M2 and M1-2 microglia (Figure 5E).
evidence: The results section describes this observation with reference to Figure 5E (likely Figure 6E) showing flow cytometry data.

claim: In both B2mtdT and Cd74tdT MOG35-55 EAE spinal cord, Olig2+ oligodendroglia were found to express tdT within EAE lesions.
source: To determine whether oligodendroglia express MHC reporters in the setting of inflammation, MOG35-55 immunized brain and spinal cord were analyzed from non-immunized baseline, pre-clinical EAE score 0 (8 days post-immunization [dpi]), and early to peak EAE (8–17 dpi) with a range of EAE clinical scores from 1.5 to 3.5. In both B2mtdT and Cd74tdT MOG35-55 EAE spinal cord, Olig2+ oligodendroglia were found to express tdT within EAE lesions (Figure 7A).
evidence: The results section describes this observation with reference to Figure 7A showing immunostaining data.

claim: The number of tdT+Olig2+ oligodendroglia was significantly higher in clinically symptomatic compared to pre-symptomatic score 0 animals in B2mtdT spinal cord.
source: The number of tdT+Olig2+ oligodendroglia was significantly higher in clinically symptomatic compared to pre-symptomatic score 0 animals (Figure 7D) in both B2mtdT (pre: 1.0 ± 0.2%, n=4; post: 6.3 ± 1.8%, n=9, p=0.0056 unpaired Mann-Whitney t-test) and Cd74tdT spinal cord (pre: 0.02 ± 0.01%, n=3; post: 0.6 ± 0.2%, n=10, p=0.0070 unpaired Mann-Whitney t-test).
evidence: The results section describes this observation with statistical analysis and reference to Figure 7D showing quantification data.

claim: The number of tdT+Olig2+ oligodendroglia was significantly higher in clinically symptomatic compared to pre-symptomatic score 0 animals in Cd74tdT spinal cord.
source: The number of tdT+Olig2+ oligodendroglia was significantly higher in clinically symptomatic compared to pre-symptomatic score 0 animals (Figure 7D) in both B2mtdT (pre: 1.0 ± 0.2%, n=4; post: 6.3 ± 1.8%, n=9, p=0.0056 unpaired Mann-Whitney t-test) and Cd74tdT spinal cord (pre: 0.02 ± 0.01%, n=3; post: 0.6 ± 0.2%, n=10, p=0.0070 unpaired Mann-Whitney t-test).
evidence: The results section describes this observation with statistical analysis and reference to Figure 7D showing quantification data.

claim: tdT+ oligodendroglia were more abundant in EAE lesion areas compared to non-lesion areas in B2mtdT EAE mice.
source: tdT+ oligodendroglia were more abundant in EAE lesion areas, determined by DAPI hypercellularity, compared to non-lesion areas in B2mtdT EAE mice (p=0.0156 paired Wilcoxon t-test, n=8) but not Cd74tdT EAE mice (p=0.1289 paired Wilcoxon t-test, n=9) (Figure 7E and F).
evidence: The results section describes this observation with statistical analysis and reference to Figure 7E and F showing quantification data.

claim: tdT+ oligodendroglia were not significantly more abundant in EAE lesion areas compared to non-lesion areas in Cd74tdT EAE mice.
source: tdT+ oligodendroglia were more abundant in EAE lesion areas, determined by DAPI hypercellularity, compared to non-lesion areas in B2mtdT EAE mice (p=0.0156 paired Wilcoxon t-test, n=8) but not Cd74tdT EAE mice (p=0.1289 paired Wilcoxon t-test, n=9) (Figure 7E and F).
evidence: The results section describes this observation with statistical analysis and reference to Figure 7E and F showing quantification data.

claim: An increase in CD45 density was significantly correlated with a higher percentage of tdT+ oligodendroglia in B2mtdT EAE sections.
source: To quantify the abundance of tdT+ oligodendroglia in relation to the degree of inflammatory infiltrates, CD45 density was quantified on whole spinal cord sections. An increase in CD45 density was significantly correlated with a higher percentage of tdT+ oligodendroglia in B2mtdT EAE sections, but not Cd74tdT EAE sections (Figure 7G), suggesting higher concentrations of MHC class I oligodendroglia in regions with higher inflammatory activity.
evidence: The results section describes this observation with reference to Figure 7G showing correlation analysis.

claim: An increase in CD45 density was not significantly correlated with a higher percentage of tdT+ oligodendroglia in Cd74tdT EAE sections.
source: To quantify the abundance of tdT+ oligodendroglia in relation to the degree of inflammatory infiltrates, CD45 density was quantified on whole spinal cord sections. An increase in CD45 density was significantly correlated with a higher percentage of tdT+ oligodendroglia in B2mtdT EAE sections, but not Cd74tdT EAE sections (Figure 7G), suggesting higher concentrations of MHC class I oligodendroglia in regions with higher inflammatory activity.
evidence: The results section describes this observation with reference to Figure 7G showing correlation analysis.

claim: Higher concentrations of MHC class I oligodendroglia are found in regions with higher inflammatory activity.
source: To quantify the abundance of tdT+ oligodendroglia in relation to the degree of inflammatory infiltrates, CD45 density was quantified on whole spinal cord sections. An increase in CD45 density was significantly correlated with a higher percentage of tdT+ oligodendroglia in B2mtdT EAE sections, but not Cd74tdT EAE sections (Figure 7G), suggesting higher concentrations of MHC class I oligodendroglia in regions with higher inflammatory activity.
evidence: The results section infers this from the correlation between CD45 density and tdT+ oligodendroglia in B2mtdT mice.

claim: The individual animal mean ROI tdT intensity was positively correlated with the individual animal mean percentage of tdT+ oligodendroglia in both B2mtdT and Cd74tdT reporter mice.
source: As an alternative measure of inflammatory activity in individual animals, the mean tdT fluorescent intensity of all spinal cord regions of interest (ROIs) imaged was used as a surrogate of overall inflammatory activity, as tdT is expressed on inflammatory infiltrates in both B2mtdT and Cd74tdT reporter animals. The individual animal mean ROI tdT intensity was positively correlated with the individual animal mean percentage of tdT+ oligodendroglia in both B2mtdT and Cd74tdT reporter mice (Figure 7H), highlighting the close correspondence between activation of MHC pathways in oligodendroglia and level of inflammatory activity.
evidence: The results section describes this observation with reference to Figure 7H showing correlation analysis.

claim: There is a close correspondence between activation of MHC pathways in oligodendroglia and level of inflammatory activity.
source: As an alternative measure of inflammatory activity in individual animals, the mean tdT fluorescent intensity of all spinal cord regions of interest (ROIs) imaged was used as a surrogate of overall inflammatory activity, as tdT is expressed on inflammatory infiltrates in both B2mtdT and Cd74tdT reporter animals. The individual animal mean ROI tdT intensity was positively correlated with the individual animal mean percentage of tdT+ oligodendroglia in both B2mtdT and Cd74tdT reporter mice (Figure 7H), highlighting the close correspondence between activation of MHC pathways in oligodendroglia and level of inflammatory activity.
evidence: The results section infers this from the correlation between tdT intensity and tdT+ oligodendroglia.

claim: Individual animal EAE clinical score was positively correlated with the mean percentage of tdT+ oligodendroglia in B2mtdT and Cd74tdT EAE spinal cord.
source: Individual animal EAE clinical score was also positively correlated with the mean percentage of tdT+ oligodendroglia in B2mtdT and Cd74tdT EAE spinal cord (Figure 7—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The results section describes this observation with reference to Figure 7—figure supplement 1A showing correlation analysis.

claim: In naive B2mtdT spinal cords, tdT+ oligodendroglia were predominantly mature CC1+ oligodendroglia (88.6 ± 1.7%, n=4).
source: To determine whether tdT+ oligodendroglia were oligodendrocyte progenitors or mature oligodendrocytes, we performed immunostaining for CC1 and PDGFRa, to identify oligodendrocytes and OPCs, respectively. In naive B2mtdT spinal cords, tdT+ oligodendroglia were predominantly mature CC1+ oligodendroglia (88.6 ± 1.7%, n=4) (Figure 7I).
evidence: The results section describes this observation with quantification and reference to Figure 7I showing immunostaining data.

claim: A minority of spinal cord TdT+Olig2+ oligodendroglia were immunoreactive to PDGFRa in B2mtdT and Cd74tdT EAE mice.
source: A minority of spinal cord TdT+Olig2+ oligodendroglia were immunoreactive to PDGFRa (Figure 7J) in B2mtdT naive (6.2 ± 0.2%, n=3), B2mtdT EAE score 0 (11.8 ± 4.0%, n=4), B2mtdT EAE score >0 (12.1 ± 2.8%, n=8), and Cd74tdT EAE score >0 (16.8 ± 4.6%, n=6), indicating that most of these MHC expressing oligodendroglia had advanced beyond the progenitor stage.
evidence: The results section describes this observation with quantification and reference to Figure 7J showing immunostaining data.

claim: Most MHC expressing oligodendroglia had advanced beyond the progenitor stage.
source: A minority of spinal cord TdT+Olig2+ oligodendroglia were immunoreactive to PDGFRa (Figure 7J) in B2mtdT naive (6.2 ± 0.2%, n=3), B2mtdT EAE score 0 (11.8 ± 4.0%, n=4), B2mtdT EAE score >0 (12.1 ± 2.8%, n=8), and Cd74tdT EAE score >0 (16.8 ± 4.6%, n=6), indicating that most of these MHC expressing oligodendroglia had advanced beyond the progenitor stage.
evidence: The results section infers this from the low percentage of PDGFRa+ cells among tdT+ oligodendroglia.

claim: The level of inflammatory activity in an individual animal was not significantly correlated with the percentage of tdT+PDGFRa+ immune OPCs.
source: The level of inflammatory activity in an individual animal based on EAE clinical score (Figure 7—figure supplement 1B), mean tdT ROI intensity (Figure 7—figure supplement 1C), or mean tdT+ oligodendroglia (Figure 7—figure supplement 1D) were not significantly correlated with the percentage of tdT+PDGFRa+ immune OPCs, suggesting that immune OPCs are not depleted in setting of more robust inflammatory activity.
evidence: The results section describes this observation with reference to supplementary figures showing correlation analysis.

claim: Immune OPCs are not depleted in setting of more robust inflammatory activity.
source: The level of inflammatory activity in an individual animal based on EAE clinical score (Figure 7—figure supplement 1B), mean tdT ROI intensity (Figure 7—figure supplement 1C), or mean tdT+ oligodendroglia (Figure 7—figure supplement 1D) were not significantly correlated with the percentage of tdT+PDGFRa+ immune OPCs, suggesting that immune OPCs are not depleted in setting of more robust inflammatory activity.
evidence: The results section infers this from the lack of correlation between inflammatory activity and immune OPC percentage.

claim: MHC reporter expression was found in some Sox9+ astrocytes in EAE lesions of both B2mtdT and Cd74tdT animals.
source: To determine if astrocytes demonstrate expression of MHC reporters in the setting of inflammation, EAE spinal cord sections were immunostained for GFAP and Sox9. MHC reporter expression was found in some Sox9+ astrocytes in EAE lesions of both B2mtdT and Cd74tdT animals (Figure 7—figure supplement 2), suggesting that astrocytes also upregulate MHC in the context of inflammation.
evidence: The results section describes this observation with reference to Figure 7—figure supplement 2 showing immunostaining data.

claim: Astrocytes upregulate MHC in the context of inflammation.
source: To determine if astrocytes demonstrate expression of MHC reporters in the setting of inflammation, EAE spinal cord sections were immunostained for GFAP and Sox9. MHC reporter expression was found in some Sox9+ astrocytes in EAE lesions of both B2mtdT and Cd74tdT animals (Figure 7—figure supplement 2), suggesting that astrocytes also upregulate MHC in the context of inflammation.
evidence: The results section infers this from the observation of MHC reporter expression in astrocytes in EAE lesions.

claim: tdT+ oligodendroglia were observed in EAE brains.
source: In addition to spinal cord tissue, we observed tdT+ oligodendroglia in EAE brains (Figure 8A and B and Figure 8—video 1).
evidence: The results section describes this observation with reference to Figure 8A and B showing tissue imaging.

claim: The number of tdT+ oligodendroglia across all brain regions analyzed was significantly higher in clinical scoring EAE animals compared to pre-clinical score 0 animals in B2mtdT mice.
source: The number of tdT+ oligodendroglia across all brain regions analyzed was significantly higher in clinical scoring EAE animals compared to pre-clinical score 0 animals in both B2mtdT (pre: 1.7 ± 0.7%, n=5; post: 6.1 ± 1.2%, n=9, p=0.0180 unpaired Mann-Whitney t-test) and Cd74tdT mice (pre: ND, n=3; post: 0.5 ± 0.2%, n=11, p=0.0165 unpaired Mann-Whitney t-test) animals (Figure 8E).
evidence: The results section describes this observation with statistical analysis and reference to Figure 8E showing quantification data.

claim: The number of tdT+ oligodendroglia across all brain regions analyzed was significantly higher in clinical scoring EAE animals compared to pre-clinical score 0 animals in Cd74tdT mice.
source: The number of tdT+ oligodendroglia across all brain regions analyzed was significantly higher in clinical scoring EAE animals compared to pre-clinical score 0 animals in both B2mtdT (pre: 1.7 ± 0.7%, n=5; post: 6.1 ± 1.2%, n=9, p=0.0180 unpaired Mann-Whitney t-test) and Cd74tdT mice (pre: ND, n=3; post: 0.5 ± 0.2%, n=11, p=0.0165 unpaired Mann-Whitney t-test) animals (Figure 8E).
evidence: The results section describes this observation with statistical analysis and reference to Figure 8E showing quantification data.

claim: The individual animal mean ROI tdT intensity was positively correlated with the individual animal mean percentage of tdT+ oligodendroglia in the brain of B2mtdT and Cd74tdT EAE mice.
source: Similar to the spinal cord analysis, the individual animal mean ROI tdT intensity was also positively correlated with the individual animal mean percentage of tdT+ oligodendroglia in the brain of B2mtdT and Cd74tdT EAE mice (Figure 8F).
evidence: The results section describes this observation with reference to Figure 8F showing correlation analysis.

claim: The EAE clinical score was correlated with the number of TdT+ oligodendroglia in B2mtdT brain, but not the Cd74tdT EAE brain.
source: However, the EAE clinical score was correlated with the number of TdT+ oligodendroglia in B2mtdT brain, but not the Cd74tdT EAE brain (Figure 8—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The results section describes this observation with reference to Figure 8—figure supplement 1A showing correlation analysis.

claim: tdT+ oligodendroglia were significantly more abundant in AT-CUP mice across all brain regions analyzed compared to cuprizone alone and adoptive transfer alone in both B2mtdT and Cd74tdT reporter animals.
source: To determine whether these MHC reporter mice are versatile enough to use with other inflammatory models, we adoptively transferred MOG-reactive Th17 T cells after cuprizone-mediated demyelination (AT-CUP) (Figure 8G), which results in inflammatory infiltrates and impaired remyelination in the corpus callosum (Baxi et al., 2015). tdT+ oligodendroglia were significantly more abundant in AT-CUP mice across all brain regions analyzed compared to cuprizone alone (CUP) and adoptive transfer (AT) alone in both B2mtdT (AT-CUP: 17.4 ± 4.6%, n=6; AT: 2.0 ± 0.6%, n=4; CUP: 0.5 ± 4.6%, n=3) and Cd74tdT (AT-CUP: 0.9 ± 0.4%, n=8; AT: 0.1 ± 0.04%, n=6; CUP: ND, n=3) reporter animals (Figure 8H).
evidence: The results section describes this observation with quantification and reference to Figure 8H showing data.

claim: The ventral brain demonstrated an enrichment of tdT+Olig2+ oligodendroglia in AT-CUP compared to cuprizone in B2mtdT mice.
source: The ventral brain demonstrated an enrichment of tdT+Olig2+ oligodendroglia in AT-CUP compared to cuprizone in B2mtdT mice (Figure 8—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The results section describes this observation with reference to Figure 8—figure supplement 1B showing quantification data.

claim: Cd74tdT mice had a significant increase in corpus and corpus horn tdT+Olig2+ oligodendroglia in AT-CUP compared to cuprizone.
source: Cd74tdT mice had a significant increase in corpus and corpus horn tdT+Olig2+ oligodendroglia in AT-CUP compared to cuprizone (Figure 8—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: The results section describes this observation with reference to Figure 8—figure supplement 1C showing quantification data.

claim: B2mtdT mice demonstrated a significantly higher proportion of tdT+ oligodendroglia in the corpus horn of cuprizone mice compared to EAE and AT-CUP mice.
source: To control for the variability of tdT+ oligodendroglia in different B2mtdT animals, due to various clinical scores and degree of inflammatory activity, we calculated the regional ratio of tdT+ oligodendroglia as a percentage of total tdT+ oligodendroglia in an individual animal (Figure 8I). B2mtdT mice demonstrated a significantly higher proportion of tdT+ oligodendroglia in the corpus horn of cuprizone mice compared to EAE and AT-CUP mice (Figure 8I, Figure 8—figure supplement 1D), suggesting that tdT+ oligodendroglia are enriched in areas of high inflammatory activity.
evidence: The results section describes this observation with reference to Figure 8I and Figure 8—figure supplement 1D showing quantification data.

claim: tdT+ oligodendroglia are enriched in areas of high inflammatory activity.
source: To control for the variability of tdT+ oligodendroglia in different B2mtdT animals, due to various clinical scores and degree of inflammatory activity, we calculated the regional ratio of tdT+ oligodendroglia as a percentage of total tdT+ oligodendroglia in an individual animal (Figure 8I). B2mtdT mice demonstrated a significantly higher proportion of tdT+ oligodendroglia in the corpus horn of cuprizone mice compared to EAE and AT-CUP mice (Figure 8I, Figure 8—figure supplement 1D), suggesting that tdT+ oligodendroglia are enriched in areas of high inflammatory activity.
evidence: The results section infers this from the regional distribution of tdT+ oligodendroglia in different disease models.

claim: Single-cell RNA sequencing was performed on tdT-positive and -negative cells sorted from Cd74tdT and B2mtdT MOG35-55 EAE brains.
source: To further define the properties of MHC expressing 'immune' oligodendroglia, we performed single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) of tdT-positive and -negative cells sorted from Cd74tdT and B2mtdT MOG35-55 EAE brains (Figure 9).
evidence: The results section describes the scRNA-seq experiment with reference to Figure 9.

claim: Clustering tdT-positive and -negative populations from Cd74tdT mice revealed mostly non-overlapping clusters.
source: Clustering tdT-positive and -negative populations from Cd74tdT mice revealed mostly non-overlapping clusters (Figure 9A).
evidence: The results section describes this observation with reference to Figure 9A showing UMAP clustering.

claim: tdT-negative cells from Cd74tdT mice were comprised predominantly of T cells, endothelial cells, oligodendroglia, and granulocytes.
source: tdT-negative cells were comprised predominantly of T cells, endothelial cells, oligodendroglia, and granulocytes, and tdT-positive cells were predominantly microglia, monocytes/macrophages, dendritic cells, and B cells (Figure 9B).
evidence: The results section describes this observation with reference to Figure 9B showing cell type composition.

claim: tdT-positive cells from Cd74tdT mice were predominantly microglia, monocytes/macrophages, dendritic cells, and B cells.
source: tdT-negative cells were comprised predominantly of T cells, endothelial cells, oligodendroglia, and granulocytes, and tdT-positive cells were predominantly microglia, monocytes/macrophages, dendritic cells, and B cells (Figure 9B).
evidence: The results section describes this observation with reference to Figure 9B showing cell type composition.

claim: The tdT-positive sorted sample from Cd74tdT mice contained high Cd74 and tdT transcript levels.
source: The tdT-positive sorted sample contained high Cd74 and tdT transcript levels (Figure 9C).
evidence: The results section describes this observation with reference to Figure 9C showing transcript expression.

claim: tdT-positive sorted cells from B2mtdT mice were predominantly monocytes/macrophages, microglia, endothelial cells, and T cells.
source: tdT-positive sorted cells from B2mtdT mice were predominantly monocytes/macrophages, microglia, endothelial cells, and T cells (Figure 9D and E), which varied in their levels of tdT and B2m transcripts (Figure 9F).
evidence: The results section describes this observation with reference to Figure 9D and E showing cell type composition.

claim: tdT-positive sorted cells from B2mtdT mice varied in their levels of tdT and B2m transcripts.
source: tdT-positive sorted cells from B2mtdT mice were predominantly monocytes/macrophages, microglia, endothelial cells, and T cells (Figure 9D and E), which varied in their levels of tdT and B2m transcripts (Figure 9F).
evidence: The results section describes this observation with reference to Figure 9F showing transcript expression.

claim: There were very few astrocytes and neurons sequenced, likely due to difficulty in isolating these populations with papain dissociation.
source: There were very few astrocytes and neurons sequenced, likely due to difficulty in isolating these populations with papain dissociation (Lo et al., 2021).
evidence: The results section explains the low representation of certain cell types with citation support.

claim: The Cd74tdT monocyte/macrophage cluster had distinct separation of tdT-positive and tdT-negative sorted cluster populations.
source: The Cd74tdT monocyte/macrophage cluster had distinct separation of tdT-positive and tdT-negative sorted cluster populations (Figure 9A) and differential gene analysis revealed enrichment of MHC class II, M2 activation, and macrophage infiltration chemokine, inflammatory signaling receptor, complement and lysosomal protease transcripts in tdT-positive myeloid cells (Figure 9—figure supplement 2, Figure 9—figure supplement 2—source data 1).
evidence: The results section describes this observation with reference to Figure 9A showing UMAP clustering.

claim: Differential gene analysis revealed enrichment of MHC class II, M2 activation, and macrophage infiltration chemokine, inflammatory signaling receptor, complement and lysosomal protease transcripts in tdT-positive myeloid cells from Cd74tdT mice.
source: The Cd74tdT monocyte/macrophage cluster had distinct separation of tdT-positive and tdT-negative sorted cluster populations (Figure 9A) and differential gene analysis revealed enrichment of MHC class II, M2 activation, and macrophage infiltration chemokine, inflammatory signaling receptor, complement and lysosomal protease transcripts in tdT-positive myeloid cells (Figure 9—figure supplement 2, Figure 9—figure supplement 2—source data 1).
evidence: The results section describes this observation with reference to Figure 9—figure supplement 2 showing differential gene expression.

source: These data indicate that MHC upregulation occurs in a minority of oligodendroglia, or that oligodendroglia that upregulate MHC are destroyed.
evidence: The results section infers this from the low representation of oligodendroglia in the tdT-positive sorted samples.

claim: Subclustering oligodendroglial cells from the Cd74tdT EAE brain resulted in nine subclusters.
source: Subclustering oligodendroglial cells from the Cd74tdT EAE brain (Figure 10A) resulted in nine subclusters (Figure 10—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The results section describes this observation with reference to Figure 10A and Figure 10—figure supplement 1A showing clustering.

claim: Several of the oligodendroglial clusters were identified as T cells, myeloid cells, and endothelial cells.
source: On further analysis, several of the clusters with oligodendroglial transcripts were identified as T cells, myeloid cells, and endothelial cells (Figure 10—figure supplement 1B–C).
evidence: The results section describes this observation with reference to Figure 10—figure supplement 1B-C showing cell type markers.

claim: The presence of myelin transcripts in T cells, myeloid cells, and endothelial cells may arise through phagocytosis of myelin debris.
source: The presence of myelin transcripts in these cells may arise through phagocytosis of myelin debris, which has been reported during development (Irfan et al., 2022; Nemes-Baran et al., 2020).
evidence: The results section infers this mechanism with citation support.

claim: After removal of contaminating clusters, 1082 oligodendroglia were distributed between eight subclusters.
source: After removal of these contaminating clusters, 1082 oligodendroglia were distributed between eight subclusters (Figure 10A).
evidence: The results section describes this observation with reference to Figure 10A showing clustering.

claim: Pan-oligodendroglial marker Olig1 and mature myelin transcripts (Cnp, Plp, Mbp, and Mobp) were present in all oligodendroglial clusters.
source: Differential gene analysis revealed that pan-oligodendroglial marker Olig1 and mature myelin transcripts (Cnp, Plp, Mbp, and Mobp) were present in all clusters, with the lowest levels of mature myelin markers and highest level of Olig1 in cluster 5.2 (Figure 10B) which was defined 'pre-OL' for intermediate oligodendrocyte, and other clusters labeled 'OL' as mature oligodendrocytes.
evidence: The results section describes this observation with reference to Figure 10B showing transcript expression.

claim: Three oligodendroglial clusters (2,3,7) were notable for the highest levels of MHC class I receptor transcripts, as well as interferon-responsive Stat1 transcription factor.
source: Three clusters (2,3,7) labeled 'class 1' were notable for the highest levels of MHC class I receptor transcripts, as well as interferon-responsive Stat1 transcription factor (Figure 10C), immunoproteasome Psmb8, peptide transport Tap1 and Cd274 transcripts (Figure 10D).
evidence: The results section describes this observation with reference to Figure 10C showing transcript expression.

claim: Expression of Cd274/PD-L1, a MHC class I inhibitory molecule, may prevent CD8-mediated killing of oligodendroglia.
source: It is possible that expression of Cd274/PD-L1, a MHC class I inhibitory molecule, prevents CD8-mediated killing of these oligodendroglia.
evidence: The results section speculates about the functional implications of Cd274 expression.

claim: Cell cycle arrest transcript Cdkn1a was highly expressed in two oligodendroglial clusters (4,6) labeled 'stress'.
source: Cell cycle arrest transcript Cdkn1a was highly expressed in two clusters (4,6) labeled 'stress' (Figure 10E), and growth arrest/apoptosis transcript Gadd45b was relatively enriched in one of these clusters (6).
evidence: The results section describes this observation with reference to Figure 10E showing transcript expression.

claim: Growth arrest/apoptosis transcript Gadd45b was relatively enriched in oligodendroglial cluster 6.
source: Cell cycle arrest transcript Cdkn1a was highly expressed in two clusters (4,6) labeled 'stress' (Figure 10E), and growth arrest/apoptosis transcript Gadd45b was relatively enriched in one of these clusters (6).
evidence: The results section describes this observation with reference to Figure 10E showing transcript expression.

claim: Cd74tdT tdT-positive sorted oligodendroglia represented 3% (34/1082) of total oligodendroglia and were found predominantly in cluster 5.1 and 5.2.
source: Cd74tdT tdT-positive sorted oligodendroglia represented 3% (34/1082) of total oligodendroglia and were found predominantly in cluster 5.1 and 5.2, which correlated with Cd74 transcript expression (Figure 10F).
evidence: The results section describes this observation with reference to Figure 10F showing cluster distribution.

claim: MHC class II transcripts (Cd74, Ctss, H2-Ab1, H2-Eb1) were enriched in oligodendroglial clusters 5.1 and 5.2.
source: Cluster 5.1 and 5.2 were labeled 'class II' and MHC class II transcripts (Cd74, Ctss, H2-Ab1, H2-Eb1) were enriched in these clusters (Figure 10G–H).
evidence: The results section describes this observation with reference to Figure 10G-H showing transcript expression.

claim: Oligodendroglial subclusters from the Cd74tdT dataset and Falcão et al., 2018 dataset overlapped to a high degree.
source: To compare our iOPC/iOL EAE subsets with a previously published mouse EAE spinal cord dataset from Falcão et al., 2018, we integrated both datasets and repeated oligodendroglial subclustering (Figure 11). Oligodendroglial subclusters from both datasets overlapped to a high degree (Figure 11A), but with several exceptions.
evidence: The results section describes this observation with reference to Figure 11A showing integrated clustering.

claim: The Cd74tdT dataset consisted predominantly of mature oligodendrocytes and did not have PDGFRa transcript containing cells present in OPC clusters of Falcao dataset.
source: Our dataset consisted predominantly of mature oligodendrocytes and did not have PDGFRa transcript containing cells present in OPC clusters of Falcao dataset (Figure 11—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The results section describes this observation with reference to Figure 11—figure supplement 1A showing transcript expression.

claim: The Falcao et al. dataset utilized an OPC reporter and lineage tracing approach, which may have resulted in an enrichment of OPCs.
source: The Falcao et al. dataset utilized an OPC reporter and lineage tracing approach, which may have resulted in an enrichment of OPCs, as opposed to our dataset which did not sort on reporter positive oligodendroglia.
evidence: The results section infers this difference in cell type composition from the different experimental approaches.

claim: One mature Falcao et al. subset, MOL3_EAE, was under-represented in the Cd74tdT dataset, which may reflect differences in spinal cord oligodendroglia compared to brain oligodendroglia.
source: One mature Falcao et al. subset, MOL3_EAE, was under-represented in our dataset, which may reflect differences in spinal cord oligodendroglia compared to brain oligodendroglia.
evidence: The results section speculates about the reason for this difference.

claim: Oligodendroglial subcluster 1-OL_homeo corresponds to primarily oligodendroglia enriched in naïve non-immunized mice from Falcao et al. dataset, which may represent homeostatic oligodendrocytes.
source: One of our subclusters, 1-OL_homeo, corresponded to primarily oligodendroglia enriched in naïve non-immunized mice from Falcao et al. dataset, which may represent homeostatic oligodendrocytes with low levels of MHC class I, MHC class II, and cell stress/apoptosis transcripts (Figure 10C–H).
evidence: The results section infers this interpretation from the cluster correspondence and transcript expression patterns.

claim: Transcripts highly expressed in the Cd74tdT oligodendroglial subclusters demonstrated high expression in corresponding Falcao et al. subclusters.
source: We selected upregulated transcripts from each oligodendroglial subcluster of our dataset (Figure 10—source data 1) and evaluated expression of these transcripts in corresponding subclusters in Falcao et al. dataset (Figure 11C). Transcripts highly expressed in our oligodendroglial subclusters demonstrated high expression in Falcao et al. subclusters, based on UMAP location.
evidence: The results section describes this observation with reference to Figure 11C showing transcript expression comparison.

claim: The analysis provides evidence of consistent MHC upregulation by subsets of oligodendroglia in the context of inflammation.
source: Together, this analysis provides further evidence of consistent MHC upregulation by subsets of oligodendroglia in the context of inflammation.
evidence: The results section concludes this from the comparison of the two datasets.

claim: MHC class I and II reporter mice enable reliable detection of immune oligodendroglia in the CNS.
source: MHC upregulation by oligodendroglia in response to inflammation may influence cell survival, myelin repair, and disease progression, but the properties of these cells, their incidence, and ultimately their fate have been difficult to study in the CNS. To overcome this limitation, we developed two new mouse lines in which the fluorescent protein tdT is expressed under control of either the B2m or Cd74 promoters, allowing identification of cells that upregulate MHC I and MHC II pathways, respectively. Our studies reveal that MHC class I and II reporter mice enable reliable detection of immune oligodendroglia in the CNS.
evidence: The discussion summarizes this as a key finding of the study.

claim: Immune oligodendroglia represent a small, but diverse population that increase in the inflammatory environment.
source: Quantitative analysis from naïve and inflammatory disease model mice reveals that these glial cells represent a small, but diverse population that increase in the inflammatory environment, mirroring single-nucleus RNA sequencing results from human MS post-mortem tissues (Schirmer et al., 2019; Jäkel et al., 2019; Absinta et al., 2021).
evidence: The discussion summarizes this finding with citation support.

claim: Immune oligodendroglia were more prevalent in areas of enhanced inflammation specific to disease pathology.
source: Although not restricted to lesion sites, immune oligodendroglia were more prevalent in areas of enhanced inflammation specific to disease pathology, where they have the potential to influence the behavior of both peripheral and central immune cells and subsequent remyelination.
evidence: The discussion summarizes this finding from the study.

claim: Immune oligodendroglia have the potential to influence the behavior of both peripheral and central immune cells and subsequent remyelination.
source: Although not restricted to lesion sites, immune oligodendroglia were more prevalent in areas of enhanced inflammation specific to disease pathology, where they have the potential to influence the behavior of both peripheral and central immune cells and subsequent remyelination.
evidence: The discussion speculates about the functional implications of immune oligodendroglia.

claim: Future, longitudinal intravital imaging of Cd74tdT and B2mtdT mice will help to define the onset and persistence of MHC activation in immune oligodendroglia.
source: Future, longitudinal intravital imaging of Cd74tdT and B2mtdT mice will help to define the onset and persistence of MHC activation in these cells and determine if they are at higher risk for removal from the CNS through cytotoxic CD8 T cell-induced death.
evidence: The discussion proposes this as a future direction for research.

claim: Future imaging will determine if immune oligodendroglia are at higher risk for removal from the CNS through cytotoxic CD8 T cell-induced death.
source: Future, longitudinal intravital imaging of Cd74tdT and B2mtdT mice will help to define the onset and persistence of MHC activation in these cells and determine if they are at higher risk for removal from the CNS through cytotoxic CD8 T cell-induced death.
evidence: The discussion proposes this as a future direction for research.

claim: MHC expression may vary with age.
source: Recent evidence suggests that MHC expression may vary with age (Nemes-Baran et al., 2020; de la Fuente et al., 2020; Mishra et al., 2020), and our scRNA-seq data revealed that a subset of MHC class I expressing oligodendroglia express PD-L1/Cd274 transcripts, which may protect these cells from CD8 T cell-mediated death and may allow MHC class I oligodendroglia to persist in inflammatory settings.
evidence: The discussion cites published studies suggesting this.

claim: A subset of MHC class I expressing oligodendroglia express PD-L1/Cd274 transcripts, which may protect these cells from CD8 T cell-mediated death.
source: Recent evidence suggests that MHC expression may vary with age (Nemes-Baran et al., 2020; de la Fuente et al., 2020; Mishra et al., 2020), and our scRNA-seq data revealed that a subset of MHC class I expressing oligodendroglia express PD-L1/Cd274 transcripts, which may protect these cells from CD8 T cell-mediated death and may allow MHC class I oligodendroglia to persist in inflammatory settings.
evidence: The discussion infers this from the scRNA-seq data showing Cd274 expression.

claim: MHC class I oligodendroglia may persist in inflammatory settings due to PD-L1/Cd274 expression.
source: Recent evidence suggests that MHC expression may vary with age (Nemes-Baran et al., 2020; de la Fuente et al., 2020; Mishra et al., 2020), and our scRNA-seq data revealed that a subset of MHC class I expressing oligodendroglia express PD-L1/Cd274 transcripts, which may protect these cells from CD8 T cell-mediated death and may allow MHC class I oligodendroglia to persist in inflammatory settings.
evidence: The discussion speculates about the functional implications of Cd274 expression.

claim: Whether immune oligodendroglia exhibit impaired differentiation and capacity for remyelination remains to be determined.
source: Whether these oligodendroglia exhibit impaired differentiation and capacity for remyelination remains to be determined.
evidence: The discussion identifies this as an open question.

claim: Oligodendroglia expressing MHC class II may be more prone to apoptosis or senescence through Gadd45b signaling.
source: Conversely, oligodendroglia expressing MHC class II may be more prone to apoptosis or senescence through Gadd45b signaling (Zaidi and Liebermann, 2022).
